name: @powerhousedao/workflow
description: Workflows in Connect: the workflow and connection document models, their editors and Workflow Studio, and the reactor piece.

config.name: PH_WORKFLOWS_SECRETS_MASTER_KEY
config.description: 64 hex chars (32 bytes) encrypting connection secrets at rest. Required on Postgres; on PGlite, unset generates a key at ./.ph/secrets.key. A key other than the one the secrets were stored with is refused, so a lost key means re-entering every secret.

config.name: PH_WORKFLOWS_EGRESS_ALLOW_ADDRESSES
config.description: Comma-separated addresses or CIDRs a piece may reach, widening the default policy that refuses private and loopback space. A bare address is taken as one host. Applies to steps and to design-time piece code alike.

config.name: PH_WORKFLOWS_RUN_CONCURRENCY
config.description: How many runs execute at once. Each slot is a forked node process, so this is the reactor's real connector concurrency.

config.name: PH_WORKFLOWS_RUN_QUEUE_DEPTH
config.description: How many runs may wait for a slot before new ones are refused. 0 waits without limit, turning saturation into latency rather than failures.

config.name: PH_WORKFLOWS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS
config.description: Cadence for a polling trigger that names none of its own. An author's override and a piece's requested schedule both win over it; a 1000ms floor applies to all three.

config.name: PH_WORKFLOWS_WEBHOOK_RECONCILE_MS
config.description: How often a webhook trigger re-registers with its provider, so a registration the provider dropped comes back.

config.name: PH_WORKFLOWS_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT_MS
config.description: How long a sync-mode delivery holds the provider's socket. Past it the run continues and the provider is told so, lest a wedged step tie up connections.

config.name: PH_WORKFLOWS_PIECE_MAX_FILE_BYTES
config.description: File-size ceiling for both directions: a FILE property hydrated from a URL, data URI or attachment ref, and ctx.files.write.

config.name: PH_WORKFLOWS_RUN_RETENTION_DAYS
config.description: Deletes finished workflow runs older than this many days, with their step executions, in an hourly sweep. On by default at 30 days; 0, "off" or "never" keeps every run, which lets the journal grow without bound.

config.name: PH_WORKFLOWS_HOST_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS
config.description: How long one call a piece makes of its host (ctx.store, ctx.reactor) may take before the step gives up on it. Raised to the step's own timeoutSeconds when that is longer. A WRITING call that times out records the step INDETERMINATE rather than FAILED, since the write may have been committed.
